item.title: Cowboys at Colts Stock Report: Caleb Downs, Quinnen Williams excel
item.description: Here is our stock report following Sunday’s Dallas Cowboys win
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys won a football game on Sunday. For real. The win was hardly the prettiest that the Cowboys have ever had, but it counts just the same as the ones that left us feeling happier than that one did. A win is a win, as they say.

While the end result was the desired one, the path there was bumpy to say the least. There were players who rose to the occasion and others who left us wanting more in several types of ways.

Let’s discuss in this week’s stock report.

Stock Up: Caleb Downs

It has felt like Caleb Downs was trending upward already, but Sunday was officially his announcement to the world. The game-sealing interception is what everybody will remember, but Downs was all over the place.

He had a critical sack on an early third down. He was credited with two passes defensed and three tackles. Simply put, he was everywhere. It was needed in the worst way.

Stock Up: Quinnen Williams

Similarly, the Cowboys officially have a new war daddy. Like Downs, Williams had really been coming along as of late.

The start to his season, his first full one with the Cowboys, was a little bit bumpy, but he singlehandedly disrupted so much of what the Colts wanted to do. We have dreamt of having a force of this nature along the interior.

Stock Up: Ryan Flournoy

It was nerve-wracking when the Cowboys announced that George Pickens would be inactive for this game. Sure, Ryan Flournoy has been very good this season, but elevating to the WR2 role is a very different thing.

Flournoy proved more than capable. He was hardly CeeDee Lamb, but he provided the necessary moments opposite of him. Dak Prescott targeted him when the team absolutely needed a spark at the end of the game.

The future of George Pickens remains unknown, but the way that Flournoy is playing is going to make those conversations very interesting to say the least.

Stock Up: Rashan Gary

Obviously there was only up to go for Rashan Gary. But he is a stock up nonetheless.

The Cowboys were able to really stifle the Colts’ offense (hardly something to be proud of, but you can only play who’s in front of you) and Rashan Gary even picked up his second sack of the season as the team kept the heat on Daniel Jones. He also contributed six tackles and two TFLs.

There has been far and few in between to choose from regarding Cowboys pass rushers this season so we have to take what we can get.

Stock Up: Tyler Goodson

Caleb Downs is obviously the best new player on the Cowboys (as in players who weren’t on the team at all last season), but Tyler Goodson has a very strong argument for number two. Goodson runs so hard and everything he does is with every bit of his energy.

Goodson averaged 6.4 yards per carry and finished with 77 yards. He has been such a breath of fresh air and is a really proper counterpunch to the attack that is Javonte Williams.

Stock Up: Christian Parker

This is also a “nowhere to go but up” situation, and the quality of the opponent is certainly worth keeping in mind. But let’s say that Christian Parker’s defense generated eight different stops on Sunday, including the one that sealed the game in Caleb Downs’ interception.

Is this representative of a turning tide? That would be a huge leap to make. But it is definitely representative of a group that is getting better and that is awesome to see.

Stock Up: Brevyn Spann-Ford

Jake Ferguson deserves a lot of kudos for the touchdown that he had in this game, especially given that it came on fourth down. To call it clutch would be to not do it due justice.

Noting that, Brevyn Spann-Ford is really making the most of his opportunities as of late. He is becoming someone who Dak Prescott clearly trusts and has assimilated well into his new role with the offense at large.

Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer

We just mentioned it, but the Ferguson touchdown really was quite fortunate. In that respect it really bailed Brian Schottenheimer out.

That touchdown came on fourth and short in the redzone, but the third down play that Brian Schottenheimer called right before it was so silly. While the Cowboys were gashing the Colts their play-caller decided to call a trick play for CeeDee Lamb that lost yardage. You can argue that the decision to go for it on fourth down, even though it worked out, was pressing a bit.

This doesn’t even cover the fact that the Cowboys barely beat a really bad Colts team. Heck, they were losing to the team in question late in the game. They almost did lose. Schottenheimer’s squad pulled this one off with zero room to spare. He has to be better.

Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey

Brandon Aubrey is still fine in an overall sense, but his trustworthiness from downtown certainly has to change. Rather the Cowboys’ trust in him has to change.

Aubrey missed a 50-yard field goal that would have given the Cowboys a 23-20 lead in this game late down the stretch. Given that it was such a deep attempt the miss gave Indianapolis the ball at their own 40-yard line and they took advantage by netting a go-ahead field goal themselves.

Stock Down: DeMarvion Overshown

Drawing an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for being out in the middle of the field when you are not even active for the game is peak silliness.

Overshown’s penalty put a drive that should have started at the Cowboys’ 30-yard line at their own 15. They wound up punting and surrendering points. Those 15 yards were consequential, even if the Cowboys wound up winning.

The Cowboys have a clear lack of a lot of things and therefore cannot afford to make silly mistakes. This was a silly mistake in the silliest of ways.

item.title: Discussion: Was the Panthers loss to the Broncos a moral victory?
item.description: The Carolina Panthers lost the game on the scoreboard, but did they win it in our hearts?
item.content:encoded:
There’s no such thing as a moral victory, right? That’s what people like to say, but I think that mindset misses a lot of nuance that can be useful when assessing the state of the team and what could be expected going forward. The Carolina Panthers lost at home to the Denver Broncos on Sunday. They didn’t put up as many points, but they outgained the Broncos and averaged more yards per play. The run defense that had been embarrassingly bad at times this season limited Denver to 3.0 yards per carry and got in the backfield on a number of plays. Bryce Young through for 276 and Chuba Hubbard averaged nearly five yards per carry. On a play to play basis, the team played well enough to win. However, untimely penalties and the flukiest of interceptions massively swung the momentum of the game in the Broncos favor, and the Panthers ultimately couldn’t overcome that. That brings us to our question…

Was Sunday’s loss to the Broncos a moral victory?

MY TAKE: I think so. The Panthers needed to show some life after disastrous outings in their last two games. The beginning of the game looked like another disaster was incoming, but the team righted the ship in the second quarter and more than held their own. The Broncos have had a weird season, but they are 6-2 and in contention for the top seed in the AFC. They’ve also got some rabbit’s foot black magic voodoo going on where they keep snatching victory from the jaws of defeat. The Panthers seemed to be victimized by that in a way yesterday. The interception was one of the flukiest I’ve ever seen, to the point where the player that intercepted the pass didn’t even realize he had an interception. There also should have been a pass interference on the play, but the officiating crew that was spamming pass interference calls all day somehow missed that one.

Otherwise, the Panthers’ undoing was a result of penalties largely from the practice squad players that are currently occupying the starting cornerback spots. And even then, I thought at least a couple of them were questionable flags. The parts of the defense that you’d want to look improved under a new defensive coordinator did look better. The offense had a good day against a very good Broncos defense. Bryce Young looked like the version of himself we saw earlier in the season and posted a season high 86.5 QBR.

The schedule lightens up significantly in the next month or so. If the Panthers play like they did today minus the penalties, they can post a good record in that stretch of games. So while the result of yesterday’s game was bitterly disappointing, I think there were enough positives to take away that we can feel good about what this team is capable of going forward.

item.title: Grading the trade: Jessie Bates gives Jaguars another playmaker, but value too good for Falcons to pass on
item.description: The Jaguars had needs at other spots, but safety was a position they wanted to upgrade. For Atlanta, the return for Bates was too good to pass up.
item.content:encoded:
On Monday morning, the trade winds kicked back up with a significant deal that will send Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Jaguars will give up a 2027 second-round selection and a 2028 fifth-round pick in return.

Bates, 29, made his first Pro Bowl in 2023 and is a three-time second-team All-Pro selection. He has one interception, three forced fumbles and a 36-yard fumble return for a touchdown this season and is entering the final year of a four-year contract he signed with Atlanta.

The Jaguars have now made a significant addition on defense, but perhaps not at the position most expected. Meanwhile, the Falcons are offloading a notable member of the secondary in spite of being half a game out of first place.

Who won Monday's trade? Let's parse through all the details of the deal.

Jaguars add major piece, filling underrated void

Following the injury to the underrated Da'Von Hamilton, it appeared that defensive tackle was the defense's most pressing and immediate need, but GM James Gladstone and head coach Liam Coen have identified another spot that needed filling first.

Safety flew beneath the radar a bit, but with Eric Murray out for the season and Caleb Ransaw currently on injured reserve, it had become a position of some concern for the Jaguars. Not that you'd know it against the likes of the Colts or the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens; the Jaguars looked like one of the best defenses in the NFL these past two games.

But when it comes time to slow down quarterbacks such as Caleb Williams and C.J. Stroud, plus whoever the Jaguars end up facing in the playoffs, it's an entirely different story. In the one game the Jaguars have allowed more than 20 points this season, Stroud and the Texans hung 34 on Jacksonville and beat them.

Bates has a lot of qualities that fit what the Jaguars seek. He's forged a reputation for being one of the league's better center fielders — and he's a ballhawk, too. Although Bates has only one pick this season, he's had multiple interceptions in all but one full season prior. He's also among the league leaders with three forced fumbles in 2026 and has 14 in his nine-year career, including 11 forced fumbles the past three-plus seasons.

The Jaguars quietly have been winning with an excellent turnover margin this season, leading the league at plus-9. In their two losses and the miracle win over the Eagles, the Jaguars were minus-1 in turnovers. This is a clear formula for victory this season, and they're trying to enhance that edge. 

It comes at a cost, however. Bates is set to hit free agency, and the Jaguars just forked over a pretty major pick with next year's second-rounder for what could end up being a half-season rental. Re-signing Bates might now be a priority, but they also must pay wide receiver Parker Washington after a breakout campaign, another quality safety in Antonio Johnson, and a few other big pieces along the lines of scrimmage, including Hamilton. 

Jacksonville's salary-cap situation is a bit tight right now, with the team currently projected to have less than $5 million in space, via Over the Cap. Two players, Trevor Lawrence and Joshua Hines-Allen, are slated to eat up nearly one-quarter of its cap allotment.

Gladstone cut his teeth under Rams GM Les Snead, and it's clear he's taking a page out of Snead's "F them picks" approach of using draft assets to secure premier players to push for a Super Bowl title. It's a bold approach, the likes of which the Jaguars previously made rarely.

It also comes at a potential cost down the road, yet it's hard not to support the move if you're a Jaguars fan. Bates has been a very reliable player in his career, missing only a handful of games, has been a four-year captain and has maintained a high level of play, even with Atlanta's defensive backslide.

It might take Bates a little time to settle in on defense, but he should be a major addition and could help solidify this secondary by playoff time. They paid up for it, but if this trade ends up helping vault the Jaguars into their first-ever Super Bowl, it could be a home-run type of addition.

Hours later, the Jaguars addressed their DT need by trading with another NFC South team, acquiring Saints DT Davon Godchaux for a late-round 2028 pick. Along with the Bates trade, the Jaguars’ defense got better Monday.

Grade: B+

Falcons lose in short term, but value was too good

On the surface, no one should bat an eye at a 3-6 team selling off major pieces, especially when those players are set to hit free agency, as Bates is next spring. But the Falcons' situation comes with a caveat: 3-6 puts them a half-game out of first place in the NFC South.

Even still, the Falcons' season has appeared a bit more wayward with each passing week, even after Michael Penix Jr. had given them a lift. There might even have been some realistic buzz even a few weeks ago after Atlanta's win over the 49ers, the first time San Francisco had lost a game.

But the Falcons, who beat the Bills and Rams a year ago, have to know that teams are not judged simply on a few impressive victories. The total package has been poor. Joe Burrow picking apart the Falcons' secondary was just the latest evidence of this team's southward turn, a week after it was humbled in the rain in Tampa.

Even with some impressive pieces, this Falcons team likely wasn't going anywhere significant this season. Bates is the ideal type of asset to trade off in this situation, given his expiring contract and reaching a point in his career where his value might start to depreciate. If the Falcons had no designs on re-signing Bates, then trading him was 100 percent the right call.

Especially given the price. Receiving a second-round pick is darned good value and above what free-agent-to-be safeties would typically earn. This feels like a seller's market, and Matt Ryan and GM Ian Cunningham deserve credit for identifying this value and pulling the trigger.

This now frees snaps for Xavier Watts, Sydney Brown and DeMarcco Hellams, allowing the Falcons enough runway this season to determine which of them belong in future secondaries. Chances are, that's a position they'll have to address in the offseason in some form, but given the draft-pick return, it was well worth it. The Falcons now have extra selections in Rounds 2, 5 6 and 7 next spring, plus all their own original selections, and are expected to receive multiple compensatory picks.

The Falcons currently have the most salary-cap space in the NFL at more than $110 million next spring, and they should have ample flexibility, even while needing to determine whether Penix remains their future and re-signing some of their own players. They took care of two major pieces already in RB Bijan Robinson and WR Drake London, so a lot of the heavy lifting is already done.

This felt like a no-brainer trade for the Falcons, even if they had to take on a little immediate salary with Bates. Getting back a plum draft pick for an expiring contract made it well worth the price.

Grade: A-

item.title: NFL trade deadline deal tracker includes Jessie Bates, Jacoby Brissett, and more
item.description: Tracking all the deals made ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is right around the corner. Teams have until 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, November 10, to make deals in an effort to either improve rosters for a playoff push, or prepare for a rebuild over the upcoming offseason.

But some teams have not waited to push deals across the line.

Monday began with the news that the Atlanta Falcons were sending defensive back Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars, as general manager James Gladstone tries to improve a defense that is already considered one of the best in the league.

While we expect more deals to come, here is a running list of the trades that have gone down so far. This will be updated as new deals come through.

Jets trade Andre Cisco to Lions

The Detroit Lions are getting some help on defense.

The New York Jets are trading safety Andre Cisco to Detroit. The safety is on an expiring contract, and the Jets — who at the moment have more than $80 million in available cap space for next year — are getting what they can now.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Lions receive: S Andre Cisco
  • Jets receive: A 2028 sixth-round selection

Saints trade Davon Godchaux to Jaguars

The Jacksonville Jaguars are not done adding to their defense.

Hours after trading for safety Jessie Bates III, the Jaguars swung a deal with the New Orleans Saints to acquire defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. While Bates can patrol the deep third of the defense and gives defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile a flexible safety that can play both in the deep middle and down near that line of scrimmage, Godchaux gives Jacksonville another option along the defensive line. That is something the Jaguars needed to add after the team lost DaVon Hamilton for the season due to a torn quad.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Jaguars receive: DT Davon Godchaux
  • Saints receive: 2028 sixth-round pick (which could elevate to a 2027 sixth-round pick if Jacksonville acquires one via trade or the compensatory selection formula)

Falcons trade Jessie Bates III to Jaguars

Trade deadline week kicked off in style with the Atlanta Falcons sending veteran safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars. For the Jaguars, it is a move to shore up the secondary as Jacksonville tries to maximize the current window of contention. For Atlanta, it is a move to get something for Bates ahead of his free agency, and with the Falcons currently looking at over $100 million in cap space, they might not receive a compensatory selection for Bates should he walk in free agency and Atlanta make the most of those resources.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Jaguars receive: S Jessie Bates III
  • Falcons receive: A 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick

Cardinals trade Jacoby Brissett to Ravens

With Arizona benching quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and the Ravens suddenly looking at life without Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley for at least the next few weeks as both are dealing with injuries, this move makes a good bit of sense. Brissett gets a chance to play on a team that is trying to stay in the playoff chase, the Ravens get a quarterback that gives them a chance to do just that, and Arizona … well maybe they could have handled things differently but they got some picks in return.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Ravens receive: QB Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick
  • Cardinals receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick

Titans trade Jeffery Simmons to Bears

Now this was a big one.

With the Chicago Bears trying to keep pace in the tough NFC North, and the defense remaining an issue, general manager Ryan Poles swung for the fences, bringing in defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons in a trade with the Tennessee Titans. Simmons paid immediate dividends, as he was stellar in his Chicago debut against the Seattle Seahawks.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Bears receive: DL Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick
  • Titans receive: A 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick, and a 2027 fourth-round pick

Colts trade DeForest Buckner to 49ers

Changes are coming in Indianapolis.

After parting ways with general manager Chris Ballard, the Colts began moving players with an eye to the future. One of those deals saw Indianapolis send DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers, returning the defensive lineman to the team that drafted him with the seventh-overall pick in the 2016 NFL Draft.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • 49ers receive: DL DeForest Buckner
  • Colts receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick

Colts trade Quenton Nelson to Seahawks

Indianapolis started their impending fire sale with a move involving guard Quenton Nelson. Still one of the premier interior offensive linemen in the NFL, the Colts sent him to Seattle as the Seahawks look to shore up their offensive line.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Seahawks receive: IOL Quenton Nelson
  • Colts receive: A 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick

Cardinals trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to Texans

It just never seemed to click for Marvin Harrison Jr. in Arizona.

Billed as one of the top wide receiver prospects in recent memory, Harrison never quite lived up to that hype with the Cardinals. Arizona selected him as the fourth-overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and after catching 62 passes for 885 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, he caught just 41 passes during 2025 and had only pulled in five receptions through the first four games of the season with Arizona.

In a move that reunited him with former college teammate C.J. Stroud, the Texans acquired him to try and give Stroud a familiar target in the passing game.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Texans receive: WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and a 2027 sixth-round pick
  • Cardinals receive: A 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick

Eagles trade Cam Jurgens to Ravens

Back at the start of October, the Baltimore Ravens swung a deal for offensive lineman Cam Jurgens of the Eagles.

The move was made to shore up the interior offensive line, in the wake of center Tyler Linderbaum signing with the Las Vegas Raiders last offseason. Baltimore’s top three centers were on injured reserve at the time the move was made, and the Ravens were using rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane in the middle.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Ravens receive: IOL Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick
  • Eagles receive: A 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick

Steelers trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys

October began with the Pittsburgh Steelers finally coming to a decision on cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Porter was seeking a contract extension from the team, but the two sides were unable to come to terms on a new deal. He also missed each of Pittsburgh’s first three games of the season due to a lingering back injury.

So Jerry Jones stepped in, acquiring the cornerback in yet another move to try and shore up a struggling defense.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Cowboys receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.
  • Steelers receive: A 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick

Vikings trade J.J. McCarthy to Giants

The first big trade of the 2026 NFL season came back at the end of September.

When the New York Giants lost quarterback Jaxson Dart to a knee injury, many wondered if the team would swing a trade for a quarterback.

Enter J.J. McCarthy. With the former Michigan passer on the losing end of a camp battle with Kyler Murray — and relegated to the QB3 spot to begin the year behind Carson Wentz — he found a fresh start in the Big Apple. And he has taken over as the team’s starting quarterback, leading the Giants to wins over Houston and Philadelphia over the past two games.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Giants receive: QB J.J. McCarthy
  • Vikings receive: A 2027 fifth-round pick

item.title: Jaguars vs. Giants Week 11 contest gets scheduling change
item.description: The New York Giants have to make an adjustment on the calendar.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants are preparing for their Week 10 matchup on Thursday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, but the league has made some changes to their schedule for the following week.

The NFL is flexing the start time for the game at MetLife Stadium between the Giants and the Jacksonville Jaguars to 4:25 pm ET instead of 1 p.m.

It is replacing the game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Philadelphia Eagles, which takes its spot at 1 p.m.

This change is largely being made for two reasons: The Jaguars and Giants are both in first place, making it one of the marquee matchups of the week. On top of that, the Eagles have struggled mightily, losing seven in a row. That streak has been capped off by the team’s most recent loss to the Giants, which sent them to 2-7 on the season.

The Steelers and Eagles have a rare in-state rivalry in Pennsylvania that doesn’t get a lot of attention because they don’t play every year. The Giants and Jaguars, on the other hand, present a much more intriguing matchup in terms of overall football competition and playoff implications in both conferences.

The Giants and Jaguars are joined in the late window by two other games on the West Coast. The New York Jets will face off against the winless Los Angeles Chargers, while the Las Vegas Raiders play a divisional matchup against Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos.

This puts the Giants front and center for the national TV game of the week on Sunday afternoon. It is a testament to how well they have played over the first half of the season, and now they will get a chance to play in front of more eyeballs.

item.title: Detroit Lions trade for veteran safety from Jets
item.description: The Detroit Lions have reportedly acquired safety Andre Cisco from the Jets before the NFL trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions are on the board for the 2026 NFL trade deadline.

According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Lions are trading for New York Jets safety Andre Cisco. In return, the Lions are sending the Jets a 2028 sixth-round pick.

Cisco was drafted in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft and spent the first four years of his career with the Jacksonville Jaguars. He played in 63 games for the Jaguars, starting 47 games for them over that time. After his rookie deal was up, he signed a one-year, $8.5 million deal with the Jets in 2025 and re-signed with the team on a one-year, $2.5 million deal this offseason.

This season, Cisco has seen his role diminished in New York after starting eight games for them last year. After starting the first three games for the Jets in 2026, Cisco has played a total of just 23 snaps with New York over the past five games.

In Detroit, Cisco should give the Lions some much-needed depth at the safety position. Brian Branch recent returned from his Achilles injury and Kerby Joseph could be on the path to returning now that his practice window has been opened up. However, the Lions have been struggling with their depth at the position. Veteran Chuck Clark has been the primary reserve and has played okay, tallying his second interception of the season on Sunday. But Christian Izien has been benched, Thomas Harper remains on injured reserve, and the Lions have scaled back the work of rookie Keith Abney, who moved to safety midseason. This move could open up the opportunity to move Abney back to nickel cornerback.

As for Cisco, he’s a versatile safety capable of playing both in the box and as a deep, coverage safety. He’ll be appealing to the Lions, because he’s an aggressive run defender. But he also has pretty good ball skills. In college, he tallied 13 interceptions for Syracuse, including seven in his freshman season. At the NFL level, Cisco has eight interceptions, 26 passes defended, four forced fumbles, and 2.5 sacks.

item.title: Jaguars trade for Saints DT to help replace injured DaVon Hamilton
item.description: The Jaguars are making their second trade on the day before the deadline, acquiring run-stuffing DT Davon Godchaux from the Saints.
item.content:encoded:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are making another trade to upgrade their defense ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline.

The Jaguars are acquiring veteran defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero. Terms of Jacksonville's deal for Godchaux were not immediately disclosed.

Godchaux is a 10-year NFL veteran who has appeared in 145 games with the Miami Dolphins, New England Patriots and Saints since being a fifth-round pick in the 2017 NFL Draft. The LSU product is a 6-3, 330-pound run stuffer and has generated 487 tackles and 5.5 sacks during his career to date.

Godchaux will help to replace DaVon Hamilton in Jacksonville's defensive line rotation. Hamilton (6-4, 335 pounds) had been serving as the Jaguars' primary nose tackle before suffering a season-ending quad injury in Week 8 against the Indianapolis Colts.

Acquiring Godchaux was Jacksonville's second trade on Monday, Nov. 9. Earlier in the day, the team made a splashier move, trading for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III to add a big-time playmaker to their secondary.

As for the Saints, trading Godchaux – who turns 32 on Wednesday – will open the door for some of their younger players to get more playing time. Third-year pro Khristian Boyd would be favored to step into a larger role in Godchaux's stead while second-round rookie Christen Miller could also see additional playing time once he returns from a toe injury.

Davon Godchaux trade details

The full details of the trade between the Jaguars and Saints involving Godchaux were not immediately disclosed.

item.title: Cam Skattebo should be ‘full-go’, J.J. McCarthy should play vs. Washington
item.description: John Harbaugh says Skattebo was “very close” to playing vs. Eagles.
item.content:encoded:
Cam Skattebo was “very close” to playing on Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles and should be “full-go” Thursday against the Washington Commanders, according to New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh.

“He was very close,” Harbaugh said on Monday morning. “We just decided to not take the risk that would go with it. There were some things that he was going to be limited just a bit, maybe. We decided not to go down that road because of the short week this week.

“He should be full-go on Thursday night.”

The Giants ran for just 80 yards on 31 carries vs. the Eagles, 2.6 yards per attempt. Devin Singletary had 21 carries for 31 yards, 1.5 yards per attempt.

Skattebo had a career-high 124 yards on 17 carries in Week 7 against the Houston Texans. He leads the Giants with 418 rushing yards on 98 carries, 4.3 yards per rushing attempt.

J.J. McCarthy ‘seems good’

Harbaugh said quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who is said to have suffered a hip pointer during the second half of Sunday’s game, is likely to be available vs. the Commanders.

“He’s doing well,” Harbaugh said. “We’ll find out more during the course of the day and in a couple of days but it does look like he’s gonna play. We feel fairly good about that but don’t want to get out over my skis with it, but it seems good so far.”

item.content:encoded:
Detroit is bringing in some secondary help.

The Jets are trading safety Andre Cisco to the Lions in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports.

Cisco, 26, is in the final season of his contract.

Cisco has appeared in nine games with four starts this year, recording 23 total tackle with two tackles for loss, a sack, a forced fumble, and a pass defensed.

A third-round pick in the 2021 draft, Cisco played his first four seasons with the Jaguars.

In 80 career games with 59 starts, he’s tallied eight interceptions, 26 passes defensed, 2.5 sacks, and six tackles for loss.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes injury update as Chiefs QB is 'day-to-day' after hurting elbow
item.description: Patrick Mahomes appears to have avoided a major injury. The Chiefs quarterback is day-to-day, according to HC Andy Reid.
item.content:encoded:
Exhale.

The Kansas City Chiefs were presented with another potential disaster scenario in Week 9, when Patrick Mahomes left the field with what appeared to be an injury. Unlike last season's torn ACL, this one had to do with the quarterback's upper body when he exited briefly with an elbow injury in the team's Week 9 win over the New York Jets.

Head coach Andy Reid met with the media on Monday, Nov. 9, where he offered a positive update on Mahomes.

“It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick,” Reid said, adding that the quarterback is day-to-day. “It looks like it’s just a matter of some rehab there and getting rid of the soreness. And we’ll just see where it goes from there.

"He’s in good spirits today.”

It was a stark contrast to the pictures that everyone saw on Sunday, Nov. 8, when Mahomes appeared to be in a great deal of pain during the second quarter. He walked off the field holding his throwing elbow after a strip-sack from Jets' rookie David Bailey.

While the news is undoubtedly good compared to the alternative, there's not yet a guarantee Mahomes will be prepared to suit up in Week 10. Reid wouldn't commit to the 31-year-old's practice availability, saying to give him some time before that decision is made.

"We'll see where he's at," Reid said. "He's feeling pretty good today. He's sore. I'm glad we're not practicing today."

Here's the latest.

Patrick Mahomes injury update

Mahomes is day-to-day, according to Reid.

It was a situation that revealed more positive news than negative in the eyes of the head coach, who doesn't appear to be in danger of losing his star quarterback. Mahomes will have to deal with some swelling and soreness, meaning it will continue to be worth monitoring as the week goes.

"If I'm able to play, I'm gonna play," Mahomes after the game. "That's part of the game. That's part of playing. It scares you in moments when you get pains in certain areas of your body.

"Obviously, I didn't feel great, but I was able to get it worked on, especially at halftime, and go out there and play the rest of the game."

Chiefs QB depth chart

  • Patrick Mahomes
  • Justin Fields
  • Garrett Nussmeier

The Chiefs do have a veteran option behind Mahomes if the star is sidelined. Fields has starting experience with the Chicago Bears, Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Jets. He is now in his sixth season and first with the Chiefs.

Nussmeier, the rookie out of LSU, has been serving as the team's emergency quarterback

item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline, but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add.

Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense.

The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else?

Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way.

As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far.

We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It’s supposed to be an active deadline, so we’ll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days.

item.title: NFL Deadline Trade Tracker: Who’s Moving in 2026?
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars have already made two additions in Week 10
item.content:encoded:
Many moves are expected over the next two days, whether or not they happen. To try to cut through the fat and keep everything contained, we’re going to launch a tracker to give you all the news from the trade deadline.

Follow along and voice your opinion on these moves in the comments section, if you have the chance.

Jets EDGE Will McDonald IV demands a trade

McDonald wants out of New York after being displaced by Kingsley Enagbare and first-round rookie Joseph Ossai. McDonald was picked right after Lukas Van Ness in the 2023 draft, when the Packers and Jets flipped first-round picks as part of the Aaron Rodgers trade.

Colts QB Daniel Jones isn’t being traded

Multiple reports are claiming that Jones won’t be moved, even though the Indianapolis Colts’ season is functionally over. Minnesota is a team that would have made sense if Jones were made available.

Falcons trade S Jessie Bates to Jaguars

Jacksonville sent a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Atlanta for the 29-year-old All-Pro safety. In the deal, the Falcons agreed to eat most of Bates’ salary for 2026. He’ll be a free agent in 2027, so the Jaguars will be able to collect a 2028 compensatory pick to backfill for their losses if they don’t spend on outside additions next offseason.

Saints trade DT Davon Godchaux to Jaguars

This one is interesting, from a Packers perspective, because Godchaux was a pre-draft visitor for Green Bay — players that the Packers usually attempt to target when available. Jacksonville needed more depth at the position after some injuries, which is why Green Bay is in the same market.

For what it’s worth, I’ve heard buzz about the Packers being interested in the running back and defensive line market. Other teams looking around at defensive tackles are the New York Giants and the Minnesota Vikings (Jacksonville seemingly called everyone for a lineman). Moro Ojomo is probably the biggest name that’s out there right now, but I’m not sure there’s an offer out there that Howie Roseman likes.

Jets trade S Andre Cisco to Lions

The Lions’ secondary needs help, and they’re getting it in the form of safety Andre Cisco. He’s being moved for a 2028 sixth-round pick, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter.

item.title: Titans, Cam Ward’s Week 10 challenge gets more complicated
item.description: The Tennessee Titans and QB Cam Ward will have a tougher challenge versus the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
The Tennessee Titans were on the Week 9 bye. Everyone is excited to watch Cam Ward play football again after his Week 8 breakout versus the Cincinnati Bengals. The Week 10 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars will be difficult and is now more complicated following their trade for Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III.

Ward was excellent against the Bengals. The sophomore No. 1 overall selection was accurate, decisive, and aggressive with ideal ball placement. Ward threw for 300+ yards for the first time in his career, and also had two touchdown passes (to Chimere Dike and Wan’Dale Robinson) for the first time this season.

Ward completed 26/40 attempts for 304 yards, the aforementioned two TDs, and zero interceptions (and a lost fumble). Here’s another fact we hadn’t seen mentioned. In addition to Ward enjoying his first-ever 300-yard throwing performance, his 26 completions tied his second-most in a single game (he was 28/42 versus the Seattle Seahawks last season). The 65% completion percentage versus the Bengals tied his previous season-high (vs. the Eagles) from earlier this year.

Ward is now tasked with building on that performance versus the Jaguars. This Anthony Campanile-coached unit is playing elite football. The Jaguars rank second in points per game allowed (15.1) and fifth in rushing (89.3). If there’s an area they’ve struggled, it’s against the pass, where they rank 22nd in yards allowed (229/game).

Hence the trade for Bates. The three-time Pro Bowl safety is among the most consistent ballhawks in the league. Bates has one interception this year, bringing his career total to 28 INTs. He ranks third among active NFL defenders in interceptions, behind just Harrison Smith and Titans legend Kevin Byard.

Bates has two career interceptions versus the Titans, including one in the painful 2021 postseason defeat. He’ll now play against the Titans twice in the coming weeks following his trade to Jacksonville from the Atlanta Falcons. Ward will have to navigate this challenge while attempting to continue improving.

item.title: Andy Reid calls Patrick Mahomes 'day-to-day' with elbow injury
item.description: Despite how bad the injury looked, Mahomes returned for Sunday's win over the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is considered day-to-day, according to head coach Andy Reid.

Mahomes appeared to suffer an elbow injury in Sunday's win over the Jets, as he was clearly in pain after a hit to his right arm.

Patrick Mahomes was holding his elbow after this hit pic.twitter.com/jyzMdNfkwR

— Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 8, 2026

When he walked off the field with trainers, he favored his arm and seemed uncomfortable throwing the ball.

Still, the quarterback returned to the game and finished it, taking hits while running and throwing the ball without a problem.

After the game, Mahomes said that with elbow injuries, it always feels scary when they happen, especially for quarterbacks.

"If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes said after the game. "It scares you in moments when you get pains in certain areas of your body, so obviously I didn't feel great. I was able to get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime, and was able to go out there and play the rest of the game."

Reid said that the injury is hopefully just one that needed rest.

"It was more positive news than negative news. It looks like it's just a matter of rehabbing and getting rid of some of the soreness."

Mahomes finished the win over the Jets with 242 yards and two touchdowns. He also ran the ball twice for eight total yards.

Mahomes has played in all eight of Kansas City's games this season. He has thrown for 2,037 yards with 14 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. The KC QB has added 85 yards and a touchdown on the ground.

Kansas City faces the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. After that, the Chiefs have games against the Arizona Cardinals, Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Chargers over the next month.

One aspect of this injury is that the Chiefs had an early bye week this year. Kansas City had a Week 5 bye, along with the Carolina Panthers, the first possible bye week in a season. Mahomes and Kansas City will have to run the gauntlet down the stretch, with 13 consecutive games to end the year.

item.title: Saints trade DT Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars
item.description: The Louisiana native is now headed to Jacksonville
item.content:encoded:
Just one day before the NFL trade deadline, the New Orleans Saints have made a move, trading defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2028 6th-round pick.

Godchaux joined the Saints in March 2025 after being acquired in a trade with the New England Patriots, which included a seventh-round draft pick to New England in exchange for the veteran defensive tackle.

A Louisiana native and former LSU standout, Godchaux returned home after spending four seasons with the Patriots. Originally selected by the Miami Dolphins in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft, Godchaux has established himself as a reliable run defender throughout his NFL career.

The trade makes sense for Jacksonville, as the Jaguars look to reinforce their defensive interior following a season-ending torn quad injury to DaVon Hamilton.

item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars weren't done trading when they swung a deal to acquire safety Jessie Bates on Monday morning.

Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports that they have also agreed to a trade with the Saints for defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. Other reports indicate a 2028 sixth-round pick will head back to New Orleans.

Bates is joining the team in a trade with the Falcons for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection.

Godchaux appeared in all eight Saints games this season and he made five starts before moving into a reserve role for the last three contests. He had 15 tackles and a tackle for loss in those appearances.

Godchaux was in his second season with the Saints. He previously played for the Patriots and Dolphins. He and Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile overlapped with the Dolphins during the 2020 season.

The Jaguars lost DaVon Hamilton to a season-ending quad injury in Week 8 and Godchaux gives them another experienced option to help fill the void.

UPDATE 1:46 p.m. ET: Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the 2028 sixth-round pick is a conditional one. The Jaguars currently do not have a 2027 sixth-rounder, but will send one to the Saints if they acquire one at some point ahead of the draft.

item.title: It’s time for the Raiders to trade Kirk Cousins
item.description: Kirk Cousins has been great for the Raiders, but even he can’t overcome the team's shortcomings.
item.content:encoded:
Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders had a bad game against the San Francisco 49ers, but to be clear, that isn’t the reason why he should be traded. Cousins, is 38 years old and playing some of if not the best ball of his career. After getting beaten the way they did on top of suffering the implosion they did, it should be clear to everyone that head coach Klint Kubiak has the team trending in the right direction. What should also be clear is that as is, the 2026 Raiders have an extremely diminutive chance of making the playoffs.

Raiders ahead of schedule but not that far

With a 4-5 record and the defending Super Bowl champions coming into Allegiant Stadium next week, the Raiders’ playoff chances are dwindling down to a mathematical permutation. The solution to that equation is a variable resting between slim and none. Cousins has had a good run, exceeded expectations and been a good bridge for both Kubiak and quarterback of the future, Fernando Mendoza, to come in and get situated.

The Raiders are not in a position for Cousins to lead them into the playoffs. Despite lining up in power formations a majority of the time, the Raiders rushing attack is non-existent. In fact, they have as many games above 100 yards (2) as they do under 50 yards as a team. Taking that a step further, after his second successful quarterback sneak for a touchdown against the 49ers, Cousins is leading the team in rushing touchdowns.

Defensively, despite a strong start, the Raiders defense stands on the precipice of being historically bad. For six straight weeks, the defense has allowed 30+ points to playoff and non-playoff teams alike. They have been the game on the schedule struggling offenses see on the calendar and circle, because they know a get-right game when they see it. Seven straight games of 30+ points against a defense has never been done in the modern era. A statistic no one should ever want to be associated with and one would be remiss if one declined to state that the Raiders likelihood of setting that record was high.

Yes, the 49ers may have had two weeks to prepare for the Raiders on both sides of the ball. But the Raiders had their opportunities to make it a game and blew chunks all over their cleats. All that to say, Cousins needs help and it’s obvious that he’s not going to get it here in 2026.

Trading Cousins

Cousins has been the dutiful soldier and if possible, should be granted the opportunity to go back where he last had meaningful success in Minnesota with head coach Kevin O’Connell. Currently, the Vikings have an extra third-round draft pick and two additional fifth-round draft picks as well. Trading carries no dead cap hit for the Raiders and the $1.6M salary fits within the remaining $6.17M of remaining cap space the Vikings have.

The Vikings have a defense, better wide receivers and a better running game. Everything Cousins needs to take the pressure off himself and contend. Although word on the street is that the Raiders may have missed their window to move him.

According to Adam Schefter, there haven’t been any offers made for Cousins, and the Raiders have had no intention of moving him. Ever the optimist, Kubiak is looking at the schedule and still sees the team as being in it, despite not having any answers for better defensive play or balance on offense. The trade deadline is Tuesday 4pm EST/1 pm PST and the Raiders only have six draft picks in the 2027 draft, with lots of holes to fill. It would behoove the Raiders’ front office to take a long, hard look at what they could get for Cousins and weigh it against the near future. Unpopular as it may be.

item.title: Seahawks expect Drew Lock to start vs. Raiders despite oblique injury
item.description: It’s good news for the Seahawks after the backup suffered an injury in Sunday’s win.
item.content:encoded:
The potential of Jalen Milroe making his first career start in Week 10 appears to have faded as quickly as it arose.

On Seattle Sports 710’s Brock and Salk on Monday, Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was asked about quarterback Drew Lock’s status, after he suffered an oblique injury in Sunday’s win over the Arizona Cardinals.

Macdonald provided an optimistic update, saying, “Good exam for Drew. He’s dealing with an oblique. And, I think it’s something we can manage in him playing the game,” while adding starter Sam Darnold would need another week in his return from his quad injury.

Lock, who entered Week 9 with what was reported as severe tendinitis, was seen grabbing his right hip in the third quarter of Seattle’s win over the Cardinals. Though he went into the blue tent, he remained in the game and didn’t miss a snap.

Macdonald told reporters post game that Lock’s status for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders was up in the air, but after encouraging news on Monday, it appears the Seahawks’ backup will be good to start a third game in 2026.

Across two starts and the bulk of Seattle’s Week 1 win over the New England Patriots, Lock has completed 71.1% of his passes, throwing for 597 yards and five touchdowns against zero interceptions.

item.title: Falcons reportedly trade safety Jessie Bates III to Jaguars for 2 draft picks, also get Davon Godchaux
item.description: Jessie Bates is reportedly on his way to the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Falcons have apparently decided to play for the future. A day after falling to the Cincinnati Bengals 34-17 in Madrid, the Falcons reportedly traded safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars for two draft picks, according to ESPN.

Jacksonville will give up a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for Bates.

Trade: Falcons are sending former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick, sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/zsvYXRXj0P

— Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 9, 2026

That wasn't the only move the team made Monday, as it also reportedly acquired New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux in a deal, according to The Ringer. The Jaguars gave up a sixth-round pick in exchange for Godchaux.

Bates has a pretty lengthy history of success in the NFL. Though Bates has made just one Pro Bowl in his career, he's been selected to three All-Pro second teams. His most recent selection came last season, when he made 98 tackles for the Falcons.

Bates, 29, is having another excellent start in 2026. Through nine games, he's registered 60 tackles and three forced fumbles. He'll take those skills to an already-dominant Jaguars defense, which is allowing the second-fewest points per game.

It cost Jacksonville a heavy price, especially considering Bates is in the final year of his contract. Barring an extension, he'll be a free agent at the end of the 2026 season.

But Jacksonville can sense the current roster has Super Bowl upside. Thanks to a tough defense and explosive offense, the Jaguars are 6-2 coming out of Week 9. While other AFC teams have been impressive, the Jaguars might have the best all-around team in the league. The addition of Bates should only help bolster that claim.

For the Falcons, the move signals the team will likely play for 2027. After Sunday's loss to the Bengals, the Falcons dropped to 3-6 on the season.

With the playoffs unlikely, the Falcons will start selling off any player who won't play a significant role with the team moving forward. Bates was the first — and could be the biggest — name traded as the team shifts its focus to the future.

item.title: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Grades, analysis and details from every key deal
item.description: We'll be tracking and grading the trades across the NFL up until the Nov. 10 deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade market is open with several high-profile deals already done. We'll be tracking and grading the trades across the NFL up until the Nov. 10 deadline.

Jets trade safety Andre Cisco to Lions

  • Date: Nov. 9

Lions receive: S Andre Cisco

Jets receive: 2028 sixth-round draft pick

Saints trade DT Davon Godchaux to Jaguars

  • Date: Nov. 9

Jaguars receive: DT Devon Godchaux

Saints receive: Conditional 2028 sixth-round draft pick

Falcons trade safety Jessie Bates to Jaguars

  • Date: Nov. 9

Jaguars receive: S Jessie Bates

Grade: B+

Falcons receive: 2027 second-round draft pick and 2028 fifth-round pick

Grade: A-

Safety flew beneath the radar a bit for Jacksonville, but injuries made it a position of some concern. Bates has a lot of qualities that fit the Jaguars seek. He's one of the league's better center fielders — and he's a ballhawk. It comes at a cost, however. Bates is set to hit free agency, and given the team's tight cap situation, he could end up being a half-season rental.

Bates is the ideal type of asset to trade off in this situation, given his expiring contract and reaching a point in his career where his value might start to depreciate. Getting back a plum draft pick for an expiring contract made it well worth the price. —Eric Edholm

Cardinals trade QB Jacoby Brissett to Ravens

  • Date: Nov. 4

Ravens receive: QB Jacoby Brissett and 2027 fifth-round draft pick

Grade: B-

Cardinals receive: 2027 fourth-round draft pick and 2028 seventh-round pick

Grade: C+

Nobody should believe Brissett will save Baltimore's season and help it win a division. But he was the best option available, and he at least makes sure the Ravens aren't playing out the string with uncompetitive football for two months. And maybe a miracle happens and the Ravens are still in contention by the time Lamar Jackson returns, if he can this season.

It's a reasonable move for the Cardinals, who are going to start rookie Carson Beck soon to get a look at him by next season. Gardner Minshew can do as well as Brissett in the short term. They get to add draft capital for a player who wasn't going to see the field the rest of the season and has an expiring contract. — Frank Schwab

Titans trade defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Bears

  • Date: Oct. 29

Bears receive: DT Jeffery Simmons, 2028 first-round draft pick

Grade: B

Titans receive: 2027 first-round draft pick, 2027 fourth-round draft pick, 2028 fifth-round draft pick

Grade: A-

Value-wise, this is close to as much compensation as you'll see moved for a defensive player. But if the Bears make a Super Bowl run, the price very well could make the move a smart one. This trade sends a clear signal that the Bears are going for it all this season.

The Titans are facing a multi-year rebuild, and this was the best way to help starting toward that effort. They have more needs today than they did yesterday, and picks are merely lottery tickets, but this felt like a deal GM Mike Borgonzi had to make. – Eric Edholm

Colts trade guard Quenton Nelson to Seahawks

  • Date: Oct. 27

Seahawks receive: G Quenton Nelson

Grade: B+

Colts receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

Grade: C+

The Colts have other players who are far less tethered to the organization who also soon could be moved. Lacking a first-round draft pick next year from the Sauce Gardner trade, the Colts are trying to recoup as much draft-pick value as possible before the spring. With Daniel Jones' struggles, along with the Colts' apparent lack of trust in Anthony Richardson Sr., the team almost certainly will be going QB hunting in the offseason. …

Given the stage of his career and his contract status, this could end up being a fairly pricy rental for the Seahawks — and that potential cost must be baked into the team's grade. But if Nelson plays to his expected level, or even above the level he's played at this season, and the Seahawks remain a title contender, it would be hard to label this as anything but a win. – Eric Edholm

Colts trade defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to 49ers

  • Date: Oct. 27

49ers receive: DT DeForest Buckner

Grade: A-

Colts receive: 2027 fourth-round pick

Grade: B-

The 49ers needed defensive help up front, and Buckner looks like the right-shaped peg for their hole inside. Osa Odighizuwa has supplied some pressure, and rookie Gracen Halton has had some big moments, but they're the only Niners DTs to play every game. There weren't many other dependable pieces inside. It was also a group that lacked length and the ability to close down passing lanes. Odighizuwa and Halton have the only two batted passes for the team this season. …

The Colts got about what could be expected in return, and considering how depleted their draft-pick drawer is with no first-round pick next year, every pick counts. Even with the 2027 selections they got for Nelson and Buckner likely falling closer to the ends of those respective rounds, the Colts are accumulating more immediate assets to compete for a quarterback next year. It's smarter than waiting a year for compensatory-pick value, even if they're having to pay for past sins. – Eric Edholm

Cardinals trade receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to Texans

  • Date: Oct. 12

Texans receive: WR Marvin Harrison Jr., 2027 sixth-round pick

Grade: C-

Cardinals receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pick

Grade: B-

Nobody outbid the Houston Texans for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. Whether that's a win for the Texans remains to be seen.

The Texans landed Harrison, the disappointing receiver from the Arizona Cardinals. It was reported Oct. 10 that the Cardinals were finalizing details on a trade for Harrison, but no team was announced. No team made a better offer to the Cardinals at the last minute, so Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round pick go to Houston for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick.

It gives Harrison a second chance. And Arizona recoups some value after a draft whiff on Harrison. – Frank Schwab

Ravens acquire center Cam Jurgens from Eagles

  • Date: Oct. 7

Ravens receive: C Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pick

Grade: B

Eagles receive: 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Grade: C+

The timing, one day after longtime Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly announced his retirement, is perhaps the most surprising element of the trade.

The Ravens, who have had a hard time replacing Tyler Linderbaum at center, recently watched as Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic all suffered injuries, forcing 2026 first-rounder Vega Ioane over from guard to center.

Jurgens now figures to be Baltimore's center for multiple seasons, given the nature of his contract after he signed an extension last year. – Eric Edholm

Cowboys acquire CB Joey Porter from Steelers

Date: Oct. 1

Cowboys receive: CB Joey Porter

Grade: B-

Steelers receive: 2027 sixth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Grade: B

Jerry Jones said before the season that he was itching to make another big trade.

The Dallas Cowboys owner made a move, with room to possibly make another splash before the deadline. Dallas dealt a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for their young cornerback Joey Porter Jr., a second-round selection in 2023.

It wasn't the all-in move Jones has teased. But it's still a big move that should help improve a defense that hasn't been great to start the 2026 season. – Frank Schwab

Giants trade for Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy

  • Date: Sept. 28

Giants receive: QB J.J. McCarthy

Grade: B-

Vikings receive: 2027 fifth-round pick

Grade: D

Is J.J. McCarthy, who fell from first- to third-string quarterback quickly in Minnesota, the answer for a Giants team that lost not only Jaxson Dart but also its top pass rusher in All-Pro Brian Burns (season-ending ACL tear)? How quickly can McCarthy acclimate to a new offense, new terminology and new cast of supporting teammates?

McCarthy played and started 10 games in two-plus seasons as a Viking, winning an impressive six. But that record often reflected the talent around him and even moreso, the strength of the Vikings' defense.

McCarthy threw 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in his 10 Vikings games. Since he was drafted in 2024, his 72.6 passer rating ranks 43rd out of 44 quarterbacks who have started at least 10 games. Only Anthony Richardson Sr., whom the Indianapolis Colts tried and failed to trade in the spring, has posted a lower mark. — Frank Schwab (grades) and Jori Epstein

Cowboys acquire offensive tackle Broderick Jones from Steelers

  • Date: Aug. 29 

Cowboys receive: OL Broderick Jones, 2027 fourth-round pick

Grade: C-

Steelers receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2027 seventh-round pick

Grade: B

There was excitement for the Pittsburgh Steelers when they drafted Georgia offensive tackle Broderick Jones with the 14th overall NFL Draft pick in 2023. They even traded up to take him.

The excitement ran out when the Steelers traded Jones to the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys sent a third- and sixth-round pick to the Steelers for Jones and a fourth-round pick.

Jones had dealt with a neck injury and had not been the player the Steelers thought they were getting. He had struggled to become a reliable tackle. He was in the mix to start for the Steelers this season but when Max Iheanachor, this year's first-round pick by Pittsburgh, made his preseason debut Thursday then Jones became expendable.

For the Cowboys, it's one of the chances they often take on players who were graded highly coming out of college but didn't work out with their first team.

– Frank Schwab

item.title: NFL moves Jaguars-Giants game in Week 11 to a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff
item.description: The NFL announced a couple of changes to kickoff times for Week 11 of the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL announced a couple of changes to kickoff times for Week 11 of the 2026 season.

The Jaguars and Giants were originally scheduled to start their game at MetLife Stadium at 1 p.m. ET on November 22, but the game will now get underway at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Steelers' visit to Philadelphia to face the Eagles was set for that time and it will now take over the 1 p.m. slot.

Both games will still be broadcast by CBS and the Jaguars-Giants contest is now set to be the network's national game during that window. It's a sensible change as both teams are leading their divisions while the Eagles, who have a bye in Week 10, will carry a seven-game losing streak into their matchup with the Steelers.

A Raiders-Broncos game in Denver will also start at 4:25 p.m. ET and the Jets-Chargers game in Los Angeles will be the lone 4:05 p.m. ET start that weekend.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes injury: Star QB avoids ‘major’ elbow injury vs. Jets
item.description: Chiefs star QB Patrick Mahomes suffered an elbow injury against the Jets
item.content:encoded:
Update (Monday): Speaking with the media, head coach Andy Reid relayed that Patrick Mahomes is “day-to-day,” and that testing showed “more positive news than negative news. It looks like it’s just a matter of rehabbing and getting rid of some of the soreness.”

The Kansas City Chiefs improved to 6-2 with a win over the New York Jets on Sunday.

But the better news for Chiefs fans is that quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided a “major injury” after hurting his elbow in the first half.

The quarterback took an awkward hit to his throwing arm with less than two minutes to go in the first half, when he was hit by New York rookie pass rusher David Bailey and lost the football. Mahomes stayed down on the turf for an extended period, before walking off with team trainers.

Here is the play where the injury occurred:

And here is Mahomes being taken off the field by members of the Kansas City training staff:

Mahomes kept his arm loose on the sidelines after the play, and returned to the game just before halftime to guide the Chiefs into field goal range. Kicker Harrison Butker missed two attempts as time expired — he missed from 56 yards but was given another chance from 51 when the Jets jumped offsides, but pushed that wide right as well — and the game went to halftime with the Chiefs leading by two.

In the second half, however, Kansas City pulled away, scoring 21 unanswered to win 35-12. Mahomes played the entire second half, and while the bulk of his throws were in the short- and intermediate areas of the field, he said after the win that “[o]nce I threw the football, I knew I was OK.”

And now tests have confirmed that fact.

According to Ian Rapoport, Mahomes underwent an MRI after the win and the scan “did not reveal a major injury.” Mahomes is expected to be monitored over the next few days for pain and swelling, but “so far, so good:”

Kansas City plays the Atlanta Falcons next week.

item.title: Seahawks rule out QB Sam Darnold for Week 10 vs. Raiders; Drew Lock dealing with oblique injury
item.description: Drew Lock is in line to start his second consecutive game for the Seahawks.
item.content:encoded:
Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald provided injury updates on the team's quarterbacks to Seattle Sports on Monday and said starter Sam Darnold will miss another week and be out for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Drew Lock is dealing with an oblique injury and had a "good exam." The team expects it to be an injury it can manage and that Lock will be able to start against Las Vegas.

Darnold missed Seattle's Week 9 win over the Arizona Cardinals with a quad injury and a cracked rib from the team's Week 8 loss to the Chicago Bears. Lock filled in and picked up the oblique issue, but it didn't keep him off the field. Backup quarterback Jalen Milroe warmed up just in case, but Lock stayed in the game.

The win over Arizona moved Seattle to 5-4, and the Seahawks are currently second in the NFC West, trailing the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers.

Darnold has played in seven games this season and has gone 3-4 in those starts. He has thrown for 1,478 yards with 10 touchdowns and 9 interceptions.

Lock has made two starts this year, and Seattle has won both. The backup quarterback has thrown for 597 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions. He hasn't run much, with just 29 yards on seven carries.

After the Week 10 game against Las Vegas, Seattle has its bye week. Darnold will have time to heal and return for a huge divisional game against the 49ers in Week 12.

item.title: Raiders expected to face Drew Lock on Sunday
item.description: Sam Darnold is out for Week 10
item.content:encoded:
Sunday night, it appeared the Las Vegas Raiders would be facing a No. 3 quarterback Sunday when they host the Seattle Seahawks.

Now, though, it seems as if they will be playing a backup.

Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald told a local radio station Monday morning that starting quarterback Sam Darnold will miss his second straight game because of quad and ribs injuries. However, Macdonald said backup Drew Lock is expected to play after he had positive news on an oblique injury. Sunday night, Macdonald indicated No. 3 quarterback Jalen Milroe could face the Raiders on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium.

Still, playing against backup is a good advantage and the Raiders, who are 4-5 and who have lost five of the past six games, could use an advantage for their defense. Las Vegas has allowed 30 or more points in six straight games. It has tied an NFL record.

Lock is 2-0 as a starter this season, with both wins coming against the Arizona Cardinals. Sunday, he completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown pass with no interceptions.
